whatItIs.text: Botanically a berry, cooked as a vegetable, and the umami backbone of world cuisine — modern uniform-red breeding bought shelf life at the cost of sweetness.

historyNote.text: The tomato's wild ancestor is native to western South America, with domesticated cultivation in southern Mexico by 500 BC; genomic studies estimate the cultivated form arose about 7,000 years ago. Spain carried it to Eurasia in the 16th century.

howToChoose.text: Choose tomatoes that smell like tomato at the stem end and feel heavy; skip fridge-cold stock and never refrigerate ripe ones — the texture goes mealy.

storage.text: Keep at room temperature stem-down, away from sun; use within a few days once fully ripe.

useItUp.text: Soft tomatoes roast into sauce, blister under the grill, or simmer into soup — the uglier the tomato, the better the jam-like roast.

substitutions.note: for cooked dishes; add a pinch of sugar for freshness
